guideposts.label: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 14 of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: Another mountain showdown is on the cards today with relentless ups and downs from Jaén all the way to the summit finish at Sierra de la Pandera: 154.5 km of racing, 4,338 metres of elevation gain! Who will succeed Richard Carapaz, the winner here in 2022? The neutral start is set at 13:15, the start proper at 13:33 after a 7.4 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

guideposts.label: Welcome to Jaén
guideposts.detail: Jaén first hosted a La Vuelta stage in 1976 (Theo Smit won stage 3) and most recently in 2021, when stage 12 headed to Cordoba. Denmark’s Magnus Cort took the fifth of his six La Vuelta stage wins. Jaén is José Manuel Diaz Gallego’s hometown. The Burgos Burpellet BH climber takes part in his third La Vuelta. guideposts.label: A province made for cycling
guideposts.detail: The province of Jaén waited for the 1976 edition to host La Vuelta but it has become a modern staple of the race. Today marks the 22nd start and 20th finish in the province that has been missing on the map of La Vuelta only five times since 2006. On the last occasion, two years ago, stage 7 of La Vuelta 24 went from Ubeda to Cazorla, where Primoz Roglic won a 2-man uphill sprint against Enric Mas.

guideposts.label: Green jersey
guideposts.detail: Yesterday, Wout van Aert took his 15th Grand Tour stage win (10 in the Tour, 4 in La Vuelta, 1 in the Giro) and received his 20th green jersey as leader of the points standings of La Vuelta (13 in 2024, 7 in 2026). He also has 20 green jerseys at the Tour de France, where he won the points standings in 2022. Van Aert is up to 224 points. His Visma-Lease a Bike teammate Matthew Brennan follows with

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: Decathlon CMA CGM face today’s challenges with a lead of 1h07’36’’ to Bahrain Victorious and 1h11’13’’ to Netcompany Ineos.

guideposts.label: The battle for the break is on
guideposts.detail: Nine riders have opened a small gap at km 3.

guideposts.label: Back together
guideposts.detail: The attackers are reeled in at km 5. It should be quite a battle before the break gets away.

guideposts.label: 24 attackers on the move
guideposts.detail: They've set off at km 9.

guideposts.label: Back together again
guideposts.detail: Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) is among the contenders for today's breakaway: “Yesterday, the feeling was good at the start, but maybe in the end I suffered a bit with the hot temperatures. For me, today and the next week are really good. But I want to think about today and this summit finish, one of the last this week, so I want to stay in front. I try to go the breakaway and it can arrive for su

guideposts.label: The battle goes on
guideposts.detail: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is already active at the front of the race. Meanwhile, his compatriot Juan Guillermo Martinez (Picnic PostNL) returns to the peloton after a mechanical.

guideposts.label: Hugo Houle abandons
guideposts.detail: There are 153 riders in the race after Hugo Houle (Alpecin-Premier Tech) abandoned and Moritz Kretschy (NSN) didn't start.

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught...
guideposts.detail: And the bunch splits due to the high pace.

guideposts.label: 35 seconds between the first two groups
guideposts.detail: The question is: who is at the front... and who is not?

guideposts.label: 41.8 km covered in the first hour
guideposts.detail: It has been a very hard battle on demanding terrain.

guideposts.label: The gap is stable: three and a half minutes
guideposts.detail: The peloton are not willing to give much of a margin to such a strong group.

guideposts.label: Knowledge of the terrain can be key
guideposts.detail: In the breakaway, we find two riders who climbed to Sierra de la Pandera in 2017 and 2022: Julien Bernard (Lidl-Trek) and David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5). “Today is going to be a very tough day, because of the heat and the finish at La Pandera, but I’ll try to get through the day as best I can, and see if I can soon get my body back on track and feel good again, because yesterday was the first

guideposts.label: The gap increases
guideposts.detail: The peloton trail by 4'10'' after 69 kilometres.

guideposts.label: A mechanical for Mas?
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard stops on the right side of the road with his teammates. The gap will get over five minutes.

guideposts.label: Labrosse abandons
guideposts.detail: Jordan Labrosse is the second Decathlon CMA CGM to leave La Vuelta 26 after Gregor Mühlberger yesterday.

guideposts.label: Oliver Peace also abandons
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, the attackers face the final 5 kilometres up the Puerto Los Villares.

guideposts.label: The gap decreases on the climb
guideposts.detail: The peloton have already moved 40'' closer to the break: 3'50''.

guideposts.label: The peloton has already gained back a minute
Results at Puerto de Los Villares (cat. 2, km 92.8)
guideposts.detail: 1. Buitrago, 5 pts 2. Fortunato, 3 pts 3. Vermaerke, 1 pt

guideposts.label: Memories from Sierra de la Pandera
guideposts.detail: Sierra de la Pandera was introduced in the 2002 edition of La Vuelta and returned in 2003, 2006, 2009, 2017 and 2022. Today marks the seventh finish at this summit. The last winner at Sierra de la Pandera is Richard Carapaz from the breakaway. Among the GC contenders, Primoz Roglic was the strongest and finished 28’’ ahead of Enric Mas and 48’’ ahead of La Roja wearer and eventual overall winner R

guideposts.label: 4 riders in today's peloton already climbed Sierra de la Pandera in 2017 and 2022
guideposts.detail: - Richard Carapaz (14th and 1st) - Enric Mas (51st and 5th) - David de la Cruz (15th ad 24th) - Julien Bernard (81st and 78th)

guideposts.label: Carapaz: "When I won, it was a bit different"
guideposts.detail: "This stage brings back some lovely memories for me, even though it was a bit different", Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) said at the start. "But I’m always keen to try and repeat the feat; let’s see how the race goes today. After all, when I won, it was a bit different and I was in a different position. I think it’s a tough day; there’ll be a lot more elevation gain. I reckon it’ll be qui

guideposts.label: Vermaerke, a tireless attacker
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) is more than a minute ahead of his breakaway rivals as he enters the final 40 kilometres. He was already in the breakaway en route to Alto de Aitana (stage 9), Calar Alto (stage 12) and Loja (stage 13), and he attacked several times in the finale to Elche de la Sierra (stage 10).

guideposts.label: The gap to the peloton increases to 7 minutes
guideposts.detail: Will it be enough for the attackers to battle for the stage win up the Puerto de Locubin and then Sierra de la Pandera?

guideposts.label: Christophe Laporte has abandoned
guideposts.detail: His team Visma-Lease a Bike reported it on their social media.

guideposts.label: 25 kilometres to go for Vermaerke
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) faces the final 4 kilometres up the Puerto de Locubin with a gap of 1'30'' to his chasers. The peloton trail by 7'50''. Someriders are dropped: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Yevgenyi Fedorov (XDS Astana)...

guideposts.label: The gaps decrease
guideposts.detail: But Vermaerke is still 1'10'' ahead of the chase group and 7'35'' of the peloton as he faces the final 2 kilometres up the Puerto de Locubin.

guideposts.label: Soon in Valdepeñas de Jaén
guideposts.detail: Valdepeñas de Jaén is famed for its steep wall (passed at km 141) that has witnessed La Vuelta stage wins for Igor Antonio (2010), Joaquim Rodriguez (2011), Dani Moreno (2013), and Primoz Roglic (2021). The Slovenian got the better of Enric Mas en route to the third of his four La Vuelta overall victories. Dani Moreno turns 45 years old today.

guideposts.label: Steinhauser catches Vermaerke up the wall of Valdepeñas de Jaén
guideposts.detail: The other attackers are just behind.

guideposts.label: Martin-Guyonnet joins Steinhauser
guideposts.detail: They are 30 seconds ahead of the chase group with 9 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: Vermaerke and Aparicio react
guideposts.detail: Their move prompts the rest of the chase group to also increase the pace.

guideposts.label: Aparicio joins the lead duo
guideposts.detail: Zana, Roriguez, Brenner, Buitrago, Paret-peintre and Sosa have accelerated. They are less than 20 seconds behind the lead trio.

guideposts.label: 5 leaders with 6 km to go
guideposts.detail: Brenner and Zana also bridge the gap. Meanwhile, Berthet and Calzoni join the Rodriguez group.

guideposts.label: Aparicio attacks as the Rodriguez - Buitrago group bridge the gap
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, EF Education-EasyPost up the pace in the GC group.

guideposts.label: Buitrago sets his pace
guideposts.detail: With 3.5 km to go, the Colombian climber catches Aparicio and drops everyone. Brenner is chasing a few metres behind. Then it's Paret-Peintre and Rodriguez.

guideposts.label: Carapaz attacks
guideposts.detail: Gall reacts with Mas and Roglic on his wheel.

guideposts.label: Brenner joins Buitrago
guideposts.detail: They are 2.5 km from the finish. +10'' Cr. Rodriguez, Sosa

guideposts.label: 4 leaders with 1.5 km to go
guideposts.detail: Rodriguez and Sosa have joined Buitrago and Brenner.

guideposts.label: Gall atacks with 3 km to go
guideposts.detail: Mas is quick to react. Roglic and Carapaz bridge the gap.

guideposts.label: Buitrago attacks into the final kilometre
guideposts.detail: Brenner reacts.

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Marco Brenner (Tudor) 2. Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious), +1'' 3. Cristian Rodriguez (XDS Astana), +11'' 4. Ivan Sosa (Kern Pharma), +14'' 5. Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step), +22''

guideposts.label: Mas and Gall have opened a gap
guideposts.detail: They catch Garcia Pierna, who helps Mas to gain time on Roglic, Carapaz and their other rivals.

guideposts.label: Gall and Mas finish 25 seconds ahead of Roglic
guideposts.detail: Carapaz drops 5 more seconds.
